speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's happening, can you tell me if these frightened awakenings seem to happen at a specific time during the night, and do you remember what happened when you woke up?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall having any frightening dreams or nightmares just before you woke up, and do you remember the details of these dreams the next day? Also, has anything stressful or frightening happened in your life recently, such as a change at school or home?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed information. Since you recall the bad dreams and aren't confused upon waking, this points more toward nightmares than sleep terrors. REQUEST IMAGES: Sleep_study_results

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any snoring, gasping, or pauses in breathing during your sleep, and have you noticed any daytime symptoms like excessive sleepiness or difficulty concentrating at school? I am asking to rule out sleep apnea, which can sometimes cause fragmented sleep and night wakings.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you recall the nightmares and there are no signs of sleep apnea or stress, this is consistent with nightmare disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder
